sections.label: COVID-19 healthcare system challenge
sections.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has challenged the healthcare system, and Singapore will keep fighting the disease while transforming health systems sustainably.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 pandemic has presented an unprecedented challenge for our healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are committed to continuing our fight against COVID-19, while also continuing to transform and strengthen our health systems in a sustainable way for the long term.

sections.label: National Centre for Infectious Disease strategy
sections.summary: The National Centre for Infectious Disease opened in September 2019, and the strategy is to prevent spread, detect cases, contain contacts and provide care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We established the National Centre for Infectious Disease, which had its official opening in September 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will press on with our strategy to fight the disease: First, to collectively prevent spread of COVID-19 through practicing safe management in how we conduct our daily activities; Second, detect new cases as early as possible; Third, contain close contacts of new cases to prevent further transmission; and finally, provide quick and effective care for patients to allow them to recover and return to their normal lives.

sections.label: Three shifts in healthcare
sections.summary: Three major shifts will move healthcare beyond healthcare to health, hospital to community, and quality to value, including preventive healthcare subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To achieve this, we will press on with three major shifts in our healthcare system, to move Beyond Healthcare to Health, Beyond Hospital to Community, and Beyond Quality to Value.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will continue our efforts to improve the diets and lifestyle of Singaporeans, and we will find new ways to do this safely in light of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will also push on with our initiatives to make preventive healthcare more affordable and accessible, such as by enhancing subsidies for vaccinations in various settings.

sections.label: Expanding healthcare capacity
sections.summary: Despite COVID-19 delaying some facilities, healthcare capacity will expand with a new hospital in the east and new polyclinics by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: While COVID-19 has pushed back the completion timelines for some of the upcoming new facilities, we will continue to expand our healthcare capacity, such as by building a new hospital in the east and new polyclinics across Singapore by 2030.

sections.label: Affordable healthcare and long-term care
sections.summary: Healthcare will stay affordable and sustainable, with ElderFund, CareShield Life, MediSave Care and a MediShield Life benefits and premiums review.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To provide better value, we will continue to keep healthcare affordable and sustainable for Singaporeans as our population ages, partnering with Singaporeans to prepare for their long-term care needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: These include three new initiatives from 2020: ElderFund, launched in January 2020, as well as CareShield Life and MediSave Care, to be launched by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In addition, we are working with the MediShield Life Council to review MediShield Life benefits and premiums to ensure that the scheme continues to provide adequate protection against large medical bills and remains sustainable.

sections.label: Attracting community care workers
sections.summary: Leadership development, scholarship programmes and salary reviews will attract more people to the community care sector and recognise healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To attract more to the community care sector, we will introduce leadership development and scholarship programmes, and review salaries for competitiveness as well as in recognition of the sacrifices made by our healthcare workers.
